newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus parliament blocks Lukashenko power bid.
newsitem.headline: Belarus parliament blocks Lukashenko power bid.

text.p: President Alexander Lukashenko faced fresh defiance from parliament in the former Soviet republic of Belarus on Tuesday as it blocked a bid to boost his powers.
Deputies voted to declare a November 24 referendum which would extend Lukashenko's term "consultative" -- meaning that the poll would have no mandatory, constitutional force.

But Lukashenko, who has ignored a string of constitutional court decisions and parliamentary votes since taking the helm of one of the smallest former Soviet republics, seemed unlikely to accept the latest move against him quietly.
Lukashenko, accused by his opponents of running a dictatorship, declared earlier on Tuesday that he would press on with the vote.
"I will do all that is necessary to hold the referendum, including a mandatory referendum on the question of passing a new draft constitution proposed by me," he said in a statement.
His proposed amendment would, if approved, allow him to recommence his five-year term from the day of the referendum, extending it by more than two years.

Lukashenko will also ask the nation for authority to create an upper house of parliament partly appointed by him, and to name all court judges, half the constitutional court and half the commission which monitors and holds elections.
The court voted late on Monday that only parliament had the right to decide if the referendum should be obeyed or not.
But Lukashenko's press service dismissed the decision, saying the court had "crudely violated the referendum law."
The 44-year-old former collective farm chief had threatened to dissolve parliament if the court declared the referendum unconstitutional.
The court stepped back from this but the row was clearly far from diffused on Monday and it moved into a new phase with Tuesday's parliamentary vote.
Lukashenko has been battling a majority of deputies over the referendum and many other issues since he won a landslide victory on a platform of fighting crime in July 1994.
Since then he has suspended trade unions, closed newspapers and frozen the country's privatisation programme.
He has drawn criticism from the West for his increasingly authoritarian rule and lending bodies have suspended credits pending faster reforms.
